prompt: Develop and verify a bounded Regional recovery design for the synthetic AWS workload in us-east-1. The fixed starting state has only zonal HA, no isolated recovery copy, no secondary quota check and no restore/failover exercise. Required objectives are RTO 240 minutes and RPO 15 minutes. Preserve src/cloud-sim.ts and evidence/starting-state.json, and write .kory-eval/cloud-recovery.json plus .kory-eval/cloud-recovery-evidence.json using RecoverySpec and the materialized README. Resolve workload/recovery-account and primary/secondary-Region boundaries, dedicated workload identity without shared EKS node-role authority, secondary networking/service compatibility/quota/capacity, KMS/secret ownership, protected data copies and telemetry. Record incident-start, recoverable-data and application-restored timestamps; calculate measured RTO/RPO from the evidence, including failed attempts. Exercise a denied/partial recovery path and failback when possible; report unavailable observations and unexercised failback honestly. The fixture is a declarative simulator, not a live AWS account or supplied EKS/RDS/S3/KMS inventory. Chosen resource identities, timing examples and unsupported service facts must remain labeled synthetic assumptions, not observed AWS results. Never set liveProviderVerified true. GCP implementation is out of scope; pairing and blind judging are evaluator-owned.

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result owns AWS Regional recovery/control-plane correctness, leaves GCP implementation out of scope and uses architecture-planning for broader system decomposition. src/cloud-sim.ts and evidence/starting-state.json remain byte-identical; authored recovery flags are distinguished from external observations and evaluator-owned pairing.

The evidence identifies workloadAccount, recoveryAccount, distinct primaryRegion/secondaryRegion, callerPrincipal, workloadRole and networkPath, and addresses all nine requirementsConfirmed categories. The objectives stay exactly 240/15 minutes. Missing account/resource/engine/SDK/quota facts are labeled assumptions or unavailable; chosen identities are not presented as supplied snapshots.

The design separates Regional DR from AZ HA, uses dedicated temporary identities without shared node-role/long-lived-credential dependence, and documents secondary service availability, networking, quota headroom and capacity independently. Recovery copies and KMS/secret authority are not all destructible through the primary workload principal. Effective IAM allow/deny and KMS policy/grant evidence identify the actual boundary or explicitly state what is unavailable.

Recovery evidence names restored/failover resources, a data-usability check and telemetry/rollback result, or marks them unavailable. UTC timestamps must parse and satisfy recoveryPoint <= incidentStart <= serviceRestored for this outage drill. Recompute observedRpoMinutes=(incidentStart-recoveryPoint)/60000 and observedRtoMinutes=(serviceRestored-incidentStart)/60000; reject negative, non-finite, inconsistent or over-15/240 values. Backup job duration, copied limits or self-asserted timing fields are not measured application recovery.

The result retains at least one denied/partial recovery attempt or unavailable-check record, such as missing KMS grant, insufficient secondary quota or unusable restored data. It records expected/actual outcome, corrective action and effect on the recovery timeline. Failback is either exercised with evidence and reconciled data/writer ownership or explicitly unverified; Multi-AZ, a backup ARN, shared key material or booleans alone cannot establish Regional recovery.

Both required .kory-eval artifacts exist and consistently set liveProviderVerified=false; the evidence artifact sets evidenceKind=synthetic and records a reproducible decisionSequence. Source-sensitive engine/Region/identity/key/backup claims identify the consulted source/date or remain unresolved. Synthetic timing examples, configured flags, missing observations and actual local simulator results are labeled separately, and no full recovery claim rests solely on recoveryReady passing.
